<user_input mode="act">Implement Step 02 of PLAN.md for HintLab in this repo (/Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon): the HintLab tutor agent built with the Cline SDK, wired into the Express server. Build on the existing Step 01 code (src/runner.ts, src/assignments.ts, src/server.ts, scripts/check-runner.ts). Do not modify anything under cline-proof/. No web UI yet.

Exact API usage: follow cline-proof/reference/sdk-check/, especially 03-real-provider-smoke.ts (ClineCore.create({ clientName, backendMode: "local" }), cline.start({ prompt, config, toolPolicies, capabilities.requestToolApproval }), createTool + zod passed through config.extraTools, cline.subscribe) and 02-clinecore-mock.ts (start({ interactive: true }) plus cline.send({ sessionId, prompt }) for follow-ups, custom config.sessionId). Install @cline/sdk (0.0.90 was verified; use that version unless it fails) and zod 4 as dependencies. Inspect the installed package's type definitions in node_modules when you need exact signatures.

Provider and credentials: the SDK must use the same ClinePass provider and model that this Cline CLI uses: provider "cline-pass", model "cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro" (check the exact provider id and model id strings the SDK expects). Work out how the SDK reads provider settings and credentials from ~/.cline (the CLI's config/data directory, already authenticated) so the server needs no API key in the repo or in env vars. Read the SDK source/types and the structure of ~/.cline to figure this out, but treat ~/.cline as read-only: never modify, copy or move anything there, and never print, log, or write any token, API key, or secret value to the terminal, to files, or to your replies (show key names or file names only, e.g. with jq 'keys' or by redacting). Make the provider id, model id and optional overrides configurable in src/config.ts (env HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID, HINTLAB_MODEL_ID) with cline-pass defaults. If authentication through ~/.cline genuinely cannot work, stop and explain exactly what failed instead of faking it.

Requirements:
1. src/agent.ts (plus helpers as needed): one shared ClineCore instance. For each session: copy the assignment into a fresh temp workdir (reuse the runner's sandbox approach) and write the student code there as main.py or main.c. Start the agent with start({ interactive: true, ... }), cwd and workspaceRoot set to the workdir, enableSpawnAgent false, enableAgentTeams false, and a system prompt saying HintLab is a tutor that diagnoses the bug and only helps through give_hint, never writing or showing corrected code. Prompts to the agent must give ABSOLUTE paths for main.py/main.c and tests.json because read_files requires absolute paths. Include the server runner's test results (inputs, expected, got) in the first prompt.
2. Tools and safety:
   - Disable every built-in file edit/write tool so the agent cannot write the fix: editor and apply_patch with { enabled: false }, plus any other write-capable or network tools the SDK exposes (check the SDK's tool list; e.g. fetch_web_content). read_files and search_codebase may be auto-approved.
   - run_commands must have autoApprove false and go through capabilities.requestToolApproval, which holds a strict allow-list of regexes and denies everything else with a reason. Only the assignment's own build and run commands in the workdir are allowed: for Python "python3 main.py" with optional "< <file>" redirect or "echo/printf ... | python3 main.py"; for C "gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main" (the tests.json build command) and "./main" with the same input forms; plus "cat main.py|main.c|tests.json". Reject anything with ;, &&, ||, backticks, $(, extra pipes, or other redirects except the allowed forms. run_commands runs on the host, so this allow-list is the only protection: make it strict and export it so it can be unit-tested. Log every approval decision as an event.
   - Never approve any other tool needing approval.
3. give_hint custom tool (createTool + zod, passed via config.extraTools, autoApprove true): input { level: 1 | 2 | 3, text: string } (an optional short tag like "off-by-one" is fine). Level 1 = conceptual nudge, level 2 = points to the area or line, level 3 = near-explicit explanation of the bug and the concept, but NEVER corrected code. Describe these rules in the tool description and the system prompt. Each give_hint call must deliver exactly the level the server asked for.
4. Server-side hint guard (src/hintGuard.ts or similar): before a hint is stored or sent to the client, reject or redact it if it contains a fenced code block (```), inline code longer than a short identifier/expression, multiple lines that look like source code, or anything that looks like a rewritten solution (for example a for/while/if/def/print/printf/scanf statement or a full corrected line of the student's program). When rejected, return an error result to the agent from give_hint telling it to rephrase without code, so the model retries; it must not reach the student. Unit-test the guard in the check script.
5. Session store: in-memory map of sessionId -> { assignmentId, workdir, current hint level, hints[], events[], status, SSE clients }. Clean up workdirs when a session ends or after a TTL.
6. Endpoints:
   - POST /api/session { assignmentId, code } (code defaults to the starter program): validate input as in Step 01, run the server runner, create the session, start the agent in the background asking for a level 1 hint, and immediately return { sessionId, testResults }.
   - GET /api/session/:id/stream: Server-Sent Events. Replay events already recorded for the session, then stream new ones live. Map cline.subscribe events (agent_event content_start/content_end for text, reasoning summaries if useful, tool calls and tool results, iteration events, errors, done) to SSE events with clear names, for example: test_results, agent_text, tool_call, tool_result, approval (allowed/denied with command), hint, hint_rejected, status, error, done. Send a heartbeat comment periodically and clean up on client disconnect. Filter events by sessionId so concurrent sessions don't mix.
   - POST /api/session/:id/next-hint: asks the agent for the next level (2, then 3) with cline.send({ sessionId, prompt }); return 409 if the agent is still busy, and a clear message once level 3 has been given. Return { level, status }.
   - 404 for unknown sessions.
7. scripts/check-agent.ts and npm script "check:agent": an end-to-end check with a REAL model call (no mocks) on sum-of-list using the buggy starter code. It must: unit-test the allow-list (allowed and denied examples, including injection attempts like "python3 main.py; rm -rf ~" and "cat /etc/passwd") and the hint guard; start the server in-process or on PORT=3200; POST /api/session; read the SSE stream; call next-hint twice; and assert that it got exactly one accepted hint at each of levels 1, 2 and 3, that no hint contains a code block or code-like solution, that no edit/write tool was ever executed, and that a denied command (if the agent tried one) was not run. Print the assignment id, each hint level and the full hint text, the distinct SSE event types seen, and the approval decisions. Use a generous overall timeout (for example 8 minutes) and exit non-zero on failure, leaving no server running.
8. Also add scripts in package.json as needed and keep "typecheck", "test:runner" working. Keep tsconfig "moduleResolution": "Bundler". Update README.md with the agent setup (how credentials are picked up from ~/.cline), the endpoints, the SSE event types, and how to run check:agent.

Port rule: another tester is using PORT=3100 right now. Use PORT=3200 for all your own server checks. Never kill, signal, or bind to processes on port 3100, and do not use broad pkill patterns; stop only processes you started (by PID).

Verify it yourself before finishing: npm install, npm run typecheck, npm run test:runner, npm run check:agent (real model call). Fix anything that fails and re-run until all pass. Then start the server on PORT=3200, do one manual POST /api/session plus a short curl of the SSE stream, and stop it by PID.

At the end, report: files created or changed, how the SDK authenticates with ClinePass via ~/.cline (without revealing secrets), the allow-list regexes, the SSE event types, and the full check:agent output including the three hints verbatim.</user_input>

metadata.systemPrompt:
You are Cline, an AI coding agent. Your primary goal is to assist users with various coding tasks by leveraging your knowledge and the tools at your disposal. Given the user's prompt, you should use the tools available to you to answer user's question.

Always gather all the necessary context before starting to work on a task. For example, if you are generating a unit test or new code, make sure you understand the requirement, the naming conventions, frameworks and libraries used and aligned in the current codebase, and the environment and commands used to run and test the code etc. Always validate the new unit test at the end including running the code if possible for live feedback.
Review each question carefully and answer it with detailed, accurate information.
If you need more information, use one of the available tools or ask for clarification instead of making assumptions or lies.

Environment you are running in:
<env>
1. Platform: darwin
2. Date: 10/4/2026
3. IDE: Terminal Shell
4. Working Directory: /Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon
</env>

Remember:
- Always adhere to existing code conventions and patterns.
- Use only libraries and frameworks that are confirmed to be in use in the current codebase.
- Provide complete and functional code without omissions or placeholders.
- Be explicit about any assumptions or limitations in your solution.
- Always show your planning process before executing any task. This will help ensure that you have a clear understanding of the requirements and that your approach aligns with the user's needs.
- Always use absolute paths when referring to files.
- You can call multiple tools in a single response. Before using tools, identify every independent read, search, command, or edit needed for the next step and emit all of those tool calls now, either as multiple tool calls or as one batched input for tools that accept arrays. Do not wait for one independent result before requesting another. Do not split independent reads, searches, checks, or edits across separate turns.
- Good parallelism examples: read all known relevant files in one read_files call; run independent inspection commands in one run_commands call; emit independent read_files, search_codebase, and run_commands calls together in one response; emit multiple editor calls together when editing different files or non-overlapping regions.
- Always verify the files you have edited or created at the end of the task to ensure they are completed and working as expected.

Begin by analyzing the user's input and gathering any necessary additional context. Then, present your plan at the start of your response along with tool calls before proceeding with the task. It's OK for this section to be quite long.

REMEMBER, be helpful and proactive! Don't ask for permission to do something when you can do it! Do not indicates you will be using a tool unless you are actually going to use it.

IMPORTANT: Always includes tool calls in your response until the task is completed. Response without tool calls will considered as completed with final answer.

When you have completed the task, please provide a summary of what you did and any relevant information that the user should know. This will help ensure that the user understands the changes made and can easily follow up if they have any questions or need further assistance. Do not indicate that you will perform an action without actually doing it. Always provide the final result in your response. Always validate your answer with checking the code and running it if possible. 

If user asked a simple question without any coding context, answer it directly without using any tools.
# Plan / Act Modes

User messages arrive wrapped in a <user_input mode="..."> tag. The mode attribute is the interaction mode the user was in when they sent that message: "plan" means plan-mode constraints applied (explore, analyze, and align on a plan -- no edits or state-changing commands), while "act" (or "yolo") means implementation was allowed. If the mode attribute changes between messages, the user switched modes -- the newest message's mode is what governs right now, regardless of what earlier messages allowed. A <mode_notice> block inside a message marks exactly when such a switch happened.

# Workspace Configuration
{
  "workspaces": {
    "/Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon": {
      "hint": "ClineHackathon",
      "latestGitCommitHash": "3575cc247890ba60821f16e45ddf8970d5051fba",
      "latestGitBranchName": "main"
    }
  }
}
